answer: Admission auction blocks bulk fake identities by selling 100 slots each epoch to the highest sealed bids. Each applicant posts one bid backed by locked credit; winners lock it 20 epochs. No velvet rope lets an insider skip the queue. Each receipt enters a shale layer tied to one cedar key, so one key buys one slot and reuse is void. The k-th fake must post a fresh bid, so 1,000 fakes lock 50,000 credits at 50 each, marginal cost rising as they outbid each other. Bid rental fails: its cedar key, shale receipt, and work history do not match. An honest agent pays once and keeps its full share.
